original_question: For the algebraic transfer tau_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H_*((Z/2)^s; F_2), F_2)^{GL_s(Z/2)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), prove or disprove the vanishing conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 whenever alpha(t) > s, where alpha(t) is the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.1 in “The problems presented by Nick Kuhn”: prove or disprove the conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 if alpha(t) > s, stated in the context of the Singer transfer tau_{s,t}. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core content of Kuhn’s problem: it is about the mod-2 Steenrod algebra, the bidegree Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), the inequality alpha(t) > s, the standard meaning of alpha(t) as the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t, and its relation to the Singer transfer. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is Problem 3.1 itself; the transfer tau_{s,t} is background context, not part of the formal statement to be proved or disproved. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The ambient algebra A should be identified explicitly as the Steenrod algebra, and in Problem 3.1 the conjecture is specialized to the case p = 2. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The paper writes the surrounding transfer in the cohomological form tau_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)^{GL_s(Z/p)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_p, F_p); your draft instead uses a homological-domain version, which is not the displayed formulation in the paper. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the conjecture is for all bidegrees (s,t), not just in a specified range. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
For exact paper-faithfulness, alpha(t) is defined as alpha(t) = k when t = 2^{i_1} + ... + 2^{i_k} with i_1 < ... < i_k. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The nearby motivation should be recorded: Reg Wood’s verification of the Peterson conjecture shows that the domain of tau_{s,t} is 0 whenever alpha(t) > s, and Kuhn is asking whether the codomain Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) vanishes in those same bidegrees; Bob Bruner had checked this in the range of known Ext computations. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
refined_question: Let A be the mod-2 Steenrod algebra. For every bidegree (s,t), where alpha(t) = k if t = 2^{i_1} + ... + 2^{i_k} with i_1 < ... < i_k (equivalently, alpha(t) is the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t), prove or disprove Kuhn’s conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 whenever alpha(t) > s. This is posed in Section 3 in the context of the mod-2 Singer transfer tau_{s,t}, whose domain is noted to vanish in those bidegrees by Wood’s verification of the Peterson conjecture. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Problem 3.1 in Section 3, not a broader question about the algebraic transfer itself. Your draft is already close, but the paper-faithful stand-alone version should explicitly name A, make clear that the conjecture is the p = 2 specialization of the surrounding Singer-transfer discussion, quantify over all bidegrees (s,t), and preserve the paper’s exact definition of alpha(t). The paragraph immediately following Problem 3.1 supplies the intended motivation: Wood’s Peterson-conjecture result forces the transfer domain to vanish when alpha(t) > s, and Kuhn asks whether Ext vanishes in those same bidegrees. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
